content:
A Cincinnati Zoo visitor has been left wondering if anything could have prevented the death of Fiona the hippo after witnessing the scene right after the hat that would kill her was accidentally flung into the animal’s enclosure.

Talking to local outlet WCPO about what he saw happen on Nov. 6, St. Louis-area resident Kevin Blaney said, “I had no idea that it was a tragedy unfolding right before my eyes.”

Blaney and his wife were planning to end their day with a stop by Hippo Cove when they walked into the habitat’s main viewing area and noticed a boy he estimated to be about 7 years old crying.

As he recalled, “There’s this little kid there who’s crying, and he’s being kind of ushered out by a lady, and she says something to him to the effect of, ‘You know, we’ll get you another [hat].’”

Blaney then noticed the hippos investigating the foreign object, which he was told ended up in their pool after the boy threw it in the air and a ceiling fan caught it, pitching it through a small gap between the viewing window and the enclosure.

“Two hippos are kind of using their noses to sort of play with it, investigate it,” he remembered. “Just putting it on their noses and kind of just moving it around with their noses.”

Blaney recognized the risk the hat could pose and went to alert zoo staff.

“They seemed very concerned, and they were getting on their radios,” he said. “I was like, ‘OK, I did the right thing.’ ”

Days later, he learned that Fiona the hippo had swallowed the hat and was in dire condition. She died on Nov. 19 after extensive efforts from the zoo’s veterinary team.

According to a necropsy, the hat had become lodged in an area of Fiona’s small intestine about 25 feet from her main digestive chamber, making it impossible to reach through surgery.

After finding out about Fiona’s death, Blaney said he asked himself, “Could I have done anything different? Obviously, I couldn’t have. It just made me think of how important it is to follow the rules.”
